Another train has double the acceleration but the same maximum speed and the same

Which velocity-time graph, on the same scale, shows the motion of this train between the same

hints: Look at the original trapezium: the rising slope is acceleration, the flat top is maximum speed, the falling slope is deceleration, and the total area is the station-to-station distance.

Double acceleration means twice the gradient $a = \Delta v / \Delta t$, so with the same $v_{max}$ the accelerating time is halved, while the same deceleration means the falling slope and its time are unchanged.

The smaller accelerating triangle removes area, so compare the flat-top lengths: the correct graph must cruise at $v_{max}$ for longer to restore the same total area with a slightly shorter total time.
walkthrough: Identify the original graph as a trapezium: velocity rises from $0$ to $v_{max}$, stays constant, then falls back to $0$.
Use the two velocity-time rules: gradient $= \Delta v / \Delta t =$ acceleration or deceleration, and area under the graph $=$ displacement, here fixed because the stations are the same.
Double the acceleration with the same $v_{max}$ gives $2a = v_{max}/t_{new}$, so $t_{new} = t_{old}/2$. The rising line must be twice as steep and reach the same peak in half the time.
Keep the same $v_{max}$ and the same deceleration, so the flat top is at the same height and the falling line has the same gradient and duration as the original.

The new accelerating triangle has only half the area, $0.5 v_{max}t_{new}$, so distance would be lost. To keep total area equal, the constant-speed rectangle $v_{max} \times t_{cruise}$ must be longer by one quarter of the old accelerating time.
That means a steeper rise, same peak, same fall, longer cruise and slightly shorter total time. This is option B.

A.explanation: The rising slope is steeper but the constant-velocity section is not lengthened enough, so the area under the graph is smaller than the original distance.

B.explanation: The rising slope is twice as steep with the same peak velocity and the same falling slope, and the longer flat top keeps the area equal to the original distance.

C.explanation: The acceleration and deceleration phases are correct in shape but the constant-velocity time is too short, so the area and therefore the distance is too small.

D.explanation: The constant-velocity section is extended too far, so the area under the graph is larger than the original distance between the same stations.
